paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The diagram displays the estimated Hessian traces, scaled by 10⁻⁵ and labeled as “Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)”, plotted against the “Rank” of adapter dimensions, which are labeled as 4, 16, 64, and 256 along the x-axis with a linear scale and no explicit unit. The y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.5, also using a linear scale. A single solid black line connects data points marked by orange squares at each rank value, starting at approximately 0.35 at rank 4, remaining nearly constant at around 0.35 at rank 16, rising to approximately 0.65 at rank 64, and further increasing to approximately 0.75 at rank 256. Each data point is accompanied by vertical error bars indicating variability.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the Hessian trace values, scaled by 10⁻⁵ and labeled “Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)”, for fine-tuned adapters as a function of their hidden dimension rank. The x-axis, labeled “Rank”, uses a linear scale with tick marks at 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the rank of the adapter’s hidden dimension. The y-axis, labeled “Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)”, uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. A single solid black line with square markers connects data points at these x-axis values: at Rank 4, the trace value is approximately 0.35; at Rank 16, it is approximately 0.32; at Rank 64, it is approximately 0.65; and at Rank 256, it is approximately 0.75. Error bars are present at each data point, indicating variability. The plot shows a general upward trend in Hessian trace values as the rank increases from 4 to 256, with a notable increase between Rank 16 and 64.
